item.title: ‘Why would he do this to us?’: Trump's foreign beef push is hurting his base, Republicans warn
item.description: Republican lawmakers warn President Donald Trump that his foreign beef import order is hurting loyal cattle ranchers ahead of the midterm elections.
item.content:encoded:
Republicans are warning President Donald Trump that his decision to flood supermarkets with foreign ground beef is hurting a key group in his base as the midterm elections near their climax.

Voters in beef-industry-heavy states, like South Dakota, Nebraska and Kansas, supported Trump in his bid for a second term. Now, lawmakers from those states say his decision to lift tariffs on hundreds of thousands of tons of foreign beef is putting the very people who elected him in a bind.

Sen. Mike Rounds, R-S.D., who is running for re-election, said his voters in South Dakota "love the president," and view him like a member of the family, but the beef import order feels like the administration "pulled the rug right out from underneath" them.

TRUMP WANTS CHEAPER BEEF. REPUBLICANS IN KEY RACES WARN HIS PLAN GOES TOO FAR

"They're hurt. I mean, they feel like they've been let down," Rounds said.

"Like, how could, you know, our friend, this guy that's as close to us as they've ever been to a president, how could he do this to them? I mean, that's the way they feel," he continued. "And that's the expression they're giving me is, ‘Why would he do this to us? Doesn't he understand ag?’"

Republicans are searching for an economic message to bring to voters as grocery bills, gas prices and other day-to-day necessities grow more expensive. Some argue that kneecapping ranchers and farmers, some of Trump’s most loyal supporters, in the name of affordability runs counter to that.

"I think people want an explanation," a House Republican granted anonymity to speak freely told Fox News Digital. "We want to be able to go to the ranchers, who are big Trump supporters, right, to be able to go to them and say, this administration is fighting for you."

THE UNEXPECTED FORCE KEEPING BEEF PRICES HIGH AND WHY THE PRESSURE COULD LAST FOR YEARS

Trump signed the order last week with the intent of flooding the market with 300,000 metric tons of imported ground beef, lowering costs for consumers thanks to a commitment that the product would be sold at 25% below current market prices over a 90-day span.

He also contended that it would allow ranchers to regrow the nation’s herds, which, thanks to a combination of drought and the invasive New World screwworm, has dwindled to historic lows not seen since the 1950s, according to data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA).

"I’m sympathetic to what he’s trying to get done," Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., told Keloland. "He’s trying to lower beef prices, which I think we’re all supportive of. I just don’t think this is the way to do it. And so, we have a lot of beef producers here in South Dakota; they produce the highest-quality beef in the world, and we’re trying to build our herds back up."

As the blowback mounts, the administration has acknowledged that ranchers are bearing the brunt of the blow. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer huddled privately with House Republicans on Wednesday afternoon, when several lawmakers pressed him on the subject of Trump’s beef imports.

NEBRASKA RANCHERS STRUGGLE TO RECOVER FROM HISTORIC WILDFIRES AS DROUGHT WORSENS CRISIS

Sources inside the room told Fox News Digital that Greer acknowledged ranchers were frustrated but maintained the import strategy was temporary. He argued it was the administration’s way of easing high prices on the market in the short term, the sources said.

But multiple House GOP lawmakers still said they were concerned as they exited the meeting.

"This is not just a one-year issue on the affordability of beef. We’ve got to make sure that we’ve got a Made-in-America-first beef program. That means standing with our cattlemen on that," Rep. Zach Nunn, R-Iowa, told Fox News Digital. "We’ve said the same thing to [Greer] in there."

Nunn, who is a top target for Democrats in November, said he planned to raise the issue again during dinner with Trump at the White House on Wednesday evening.

Rep. Troy Downing, R-Mont., pointed out that it was a relatively small amount of beef for just a 90-day period but said he was worried about the timing as it overlaps with the time of year farmers bring their cattle to market.

"If a rancher is expecting to get a price at market that suddenly drops out from underneath them, they’re faced with two things — they don’t have a stable market, so do I invest in heifers for next year? Or do I have to sell more calves to make up for that deficit for my operating costs? Which, neither one is helping rebuild the herd," Downing told Fox News Digital.

House Main Street Caucus Chairman Mike Flood, R-Neb., said he was opposed to a "tariff regime that undercuts American ranchers," but said Trump’s policies were helping in the "big picture."

Compounding people’s anxiety in the meeting was Trump’s trade war with Canada, which that House Republican said made northern-border-state GOP lawmakers "nervous."

Republican Study Committee Chairman August Pfluger, R-Texas, told Fox News Digital there would likely be "quite a few" follow-up meetings.

"It was absolutely outstanding, we had a tremendous amount of participation and people that were really excited to ask good questions," he said of the meeting in general.

And Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said at an event in Iowa on Tuesday that the administration understood that "ranchers felt like that was a gut punch."

The White House argued that Trump "has done more for American agriculture than anyone" with trade deals, foreign market access expansion, lowering input costs, bolstering the farm safety net, doubling the death tax exemption, ending taxes on rural property loan interest, and creating rural opportunity zones."

"At the same time, he is delivering on his promise to consumers by reducing beef prices while allowing our American beef herd to grow," White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly told Fox News Digital. "The President will continue taking actions to support our great farmers while driving economic prosperity for all Americans."

Republican critics of the move are urging the administration to look at other methods to expand the nation’s cattle herds.

Several Republicans, led by Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., wrote to Rollins and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to lift Biden-era rules and ease federal guardrails to allow for more access to grazing land for cattle.

"The Federal government must remain laser-focused on partnering with the industry and state efforts for ranchers, expand grazing on public and private lands, and improve protein processing capacity," they wrote in a letter to the top Trump officials on Tuesday.

item.title: Chase Elliott says NASCAR's grueling 10-month season can 'eat you up' without an escape
item.description: Chase Elliott reveals how fly fishing, golf, snowboarding and hiking in Colorado help him survive NASCAR's grueling February-to-November schedule.
item.content:encoded:
Chase Elliott spends most of his year trying to go faster than everyone else.

So when he finally gets a chance to slow down, you'll probably find him with a fly rod, on a golf course, hiking somewhere in Colorado or strapped to a snowboard.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

And according to the former NASCAR Cup Series champion, those escapes aren't just a nice way to kill time between races. They're almost a necessity.

NASCAR's schedule is a grind. But Elliott says it's not necessarily the number of races that wears on drivers — it's how much of the calendar the season consumes.

"You tell people, ‘Oh, well how many races are in a year?’ And you say, ‘Well, there’s 38,’ and they’re like, ‘Oh wow, that’s a lot,’" Elliott told OutKick OutDoors. "But in my mind, it’s not. It’s not the 38 races that’s a lot. It’s the time span from February to November."

That's nearly the entire year spent traveling, preparing, racing and trying to keep pace in one of the most competitive garages in motorsports.

And Elliott believes drivers who don't find some way to occasionally get away from it can pay the price.

"If you don't have ways to escape and ways to reset and do the things that you need to do to show up with the right mindset, I think it has a high potential to really eat you up," he said. "Especially when things aren't going good."

Watch Chase Elliott's full interview with OutKick OutDoors here:

For Elliott, a lot of that reset happens outdoors.

He's an avid fly fisherman, a hobby he picked up after growing up around his dad's best friend and his uncle Ernie, who were both heavily into the sport.

And part of the appeal is that it's really freaking hard.

Elliott has previously compared fly fishing to golf — another hobby he loves, despite admitting he's still waiting for the part where he actually gets good at it.

The similarities, he explained, are everywhere.

THE BEST OUTDOOR WEEKEND IN NORTHWEST GEORGIA DOESN’T REQUIRE 'ROUGHING IT' OR SLEEPING ON THE GROUND

Lay a fly down too aggressively and you can scare off the fish. Try to cast through the heavily wooded streams of North Georgia and there's a decent chance you'll spend part of your day retrieving hooks from trees. Even when everything goes right, you're still chasing a level of mastery that may never actually come.

"It's just the craft of being good at it, and kind of that never-ending journey and never-ending search of trying to master something that will never be mastered," Elliott said. "And I think those two things fall in that category."

Golf has presented a similar problem.

Elliott said he used to be more competitive about the game and still occasionally goes through stretches where he decides he's finally going to figure it out.

Then reality intervenes.

"I'm very one-track-minded, I think, in a lot of ways," he said.

To attack golf the way he'd need to in order to become genuinely good, Elliott believes he'd have to take time and attention away from other parts of his life — most notably his actual job.

So, for now, he's content to remain hopelessly in pursuit.

"Hopefully there will be a day and a time that I can commit to things that I want to get better at or want to try and master," he said.

His love of being outside goes well beyond fishing and golf, though.

Elliott spent a couple of years living in Colorado as a kid after his father, NASCAR Hall of Famer Bill Elliott, stepped away from full-time racing. Looking back, he considers those years a gift.

"If you were bored, it was your own fault," Elliott said.

While kids elsewhere might have spent afternoons parked in front of an Xbox or PlayStation, Elliott remembers his Colorado childhood differently.

"It was just all outside, all we could do," he said.

DENNY HAMLIN CHASES MONSTER LARGEMOUTH BASS IN TEXAS WITH BASSMASTER PRO CHRIS ZALDAIN

Summers offered seemingly endless options. Winters meant snowboarding and skiing. And if riding the chairlift got boring, Elliott and his buddies would hike farther up the mountain in search of fresh tracks no one else wanted to work for.

He still tries to get back to Colorado when NASCAR's schedule makes it possible, sometimes taking advantage of western race swings rather than flying all the way home to the East Coast just to turn around again.

Snowboarding remains one of his favorite ways to stay active, too — especially when getting to the good stuff requires hiking rather than simply hopping off a lift.

But no matter the activity, the purpose is largely the same.

For a driver whose professional life stretches from February through November, there has to be something beyond the next race.

That's not to say Elliott checks out. Quite the opposite.

He said he feels a responsibility to his team to make sure he's doing everything asked of him at the highest level, especially because he knows the people around him are doing the same.

But being completely consumed by racing isn't necessarily the best way to accomplish that.

"I think for all of us, it's important to break away when you can," Elliott said. "And I think it's good for the whole environment."

He's right, and it's true for everyone — you, me and even your favorite NASCAR driver. Every once in a while, you just have to slow down.

item.title: Tens of thousands flood streets to protest Spain border crisis
item.description: Tens of thousands protested Pedro Sanchez across Spain as 50,000 marched in Madrid over the migrant crisis in Ceuta following July's border surge.
item.content:encoded:
Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across Spain to protest the government's handling of a mass crossing of migrants into Spain in July.

Authorities say 50,000 protesters were on the streets in Madrid alone, furious at Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez as the migrant crisis in Spain's North African city of Ceuta continues.

Violence continued for hours after the major protests ended, with gunshots and explosions audible throughout the night on Wednesday.

SPAIN STOCKS AFRICAN ENCLAVE CEUTA WITH BOOSTED SECURITY AS MOROCCO MONITORS CALLS FOR SECOND BORDER RUSH

The protesters bore signs reading, "A united Ceuta will never be defeated," "Sánchez to prison," and "Invaders — go home!"

Spain is still dealing with the fallout after over 70,000 foreign migrants surged across its border from neighboring Morocco in late July.

AT LEAST 72 DEAD AMID MASS MIGRANT RUSH TO STORM SPANISH ENCLAVE OF CEUTA SPARKING BORDER CRISIS

Thousands of those migrants remain in Spanish territory even now.

"What happened to us was not a migratory crisis," Ceuta's regional leader, Juan Jesús Vivas, said Wednesday. "What happened was the violation of Spain's territorial integrity."

SOCIALIST SPANISH PM BLASTS MELONI OVER RESTORED BORDER CONTROLS AFTER CEUTA SURGE, DEMANDS EMERGENCY MEETING

The protests came days after Ceuta residents tore down and burned makeshift migrant shelters found in their city.

Demonstrators carrying Spanish flags moved toward beachside migrant camps last week, destroying shelters and setting fires as police attempted to keep protesters and migrants apart, according to Spain’s public broadcaster RTVE and news agency EFE.

SPAIN DEPLOYS MILITARY AFTER THOUSANDS OF MIGRANTS OVERWHELM BORDER ENCLAVE, AT LEAST 18 DEAD

Meanwhile, Sanchez has blamed Russia and Israel for amplifying the migrant crisis via social media, saying the July surge across the border was due to a misinterpretation of a Spanish Supreme Court ruling.

Sánchez told radio station SER that research by the European Union’s diplomatic service, the European External Action Service, indicated Russian and Israeli networks had participated in spreading disinformation alongside far-right networks, Reuters reported Aug. 31.

"Without facts, without materials backed up by numbers, dates, names, there is simply nothing to talk about," Russia's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova told reporters.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar accused Sánchez of "lying shamelessly," and said in a post on X that the Spanish leader was attempting to divert attention from domestic policy failures.

Fox News' Efrat Lachter and the Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: FIRST ON FOX: ‘No Kings’ protest network behind fight against AI data centers and Flock cameras
item.description: Fox News Digital traces how pro-China socialist groups moved from anti-Trump, anti-Israel protests into technology messages that spread to conservatives and libertarians.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: The same hard-left network behind "No Kings" and other protests is leading the battle against data centers and Flock surveillance cameras, according to a Fox News Digital investigation and a new report.

In growing protests from San Francisco to North Carolina, organizations and activists associated with the same ecosystem that rallied against President Donald Trump, Israel, Elon Musk, Tesla and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) over the last two years are now taking on data-center construction and license-plate readers.

The overlap includes organizations funded by pro-China, Shanghai-based tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham, whose sprawling nonprofit and media network has faced Congressional and federal scrutiny over its funding and foreign ties. Singham and the nonprofits he has funded have denied taking orders from any government or political party and haven’t been charged with any crimes.

INSIDE THE FAR-LEFT'S ANTI-DATA CENTER PUSH AND WHAT EXPERTS SAY IS DRIVING IT: 'PLAYBOOK WE'VE SEEN BEFORE'

The findings are detailed in a new report, "The Compute War at Home," commissioned by Consumer Action for a Strong Economy, an Alexandria, Va., free-markets nonprofit that used social-media analysis by Arken Intelligence, a technology firm based in Washington, D.C., for parts of its study.

"The money, media, organizing capacity and campaign objectives converge in the same ecosystem," the report says.

Based on reporting over the past several years from street protests, Fox News Digital has identified the protest movement’s evolution across three phases. The new report chronicles a repeatable political model, in which activists first identify a local grievance, then connect it to a larger ideological narrative and package the argument through national media and activist infrastructure and carry it into new communities.

The first phase appeared in early January 2025 with Trump’s inauguration and the launch of "Tesla Takedown" demonstrations to protest Tesla founder Musk as he led efforts to cut waste in federal spending. It became the mobilization infrastructure built around "No Kings" and "Hands Off" anti-Trump protests, anti-Israel activism and related campaigns, supporting the Communist Party of Cuba, the Islamic Republic of Iran and Venezuelan communist strongman Nicholas Maduro.

Organizations from the Singham network – including the Party for Socialism and Liberation, CodePink, the People’s Forum, ANSWER Coalition and affiliated groups – appeared repeatedly across those movements, working with nonprofits more aligned with the Democratic Party, including Indivisible, a nonprofit network funded in part by billionaire Democratic megadonor George Soros. The organizations deny any wrongdoing as agents of alleged foreign influence and say they are addressing legitimate community grievances.

AGITATORS UNITED BY CHINESE MONEY, HATE FOR AMERICA TARGET DATA CENTERS, EXPERTS WARN

The second phase shifted that protest infrastructure toward American technological infrastructure. Over the past year, CodePink developed a national campaign against data centers, while the campaign took root among the approximately 70 chapters of the Party for Socialism and Liberation with near-identical messaging and strategies. Liberation News, which describes itself as the newspaper of the Party for Socialism and Liberation, nationalized local victories and promoted moratoria, bans and project cancellations. Media outlets, like BreathThrough News, from the Singham network provided additional amplification.

The third phase involved an ideological crossover in which Flock cameras have now become a bridge between local privacy and policing concerns and the national fight over artificial intelligence, cloud systems, energy and data centers.

The report doesn’t claim that every opponent of Flock cameras or data centers is connected to the activist network. It notes that opposition to Flock has become genuinely bipartisan, with legitimate concerns about privacy, data retention, misuse and poorly written government contracts. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis recently ordered license-plate readers removed from state highways, while Texas has also moved to pull back from the technology, and Republican Sen. Josh Hawley has launched an investigation into Flock cameras over surveillance concerns.

But the report credits the left-wing organizers with fusing the two issues into a one-two punch that has caught on with a broad coalition.

According to the Arken Intelligence analysis, posts mentioning both Flock and data centers increased from 639 posts in the 10 weeks before a spike in organizing on May 19 led to 9,009 posts over the next 10 weeks, a 14.1-fold increase.

Among posts for which a political affiliation could be classified, the report said, 81% came from right-wing, conservative or libertarian accounts.

"Issue pairings rarely multiply fourteen-fold in a matter of weeks without a catalyst, particularly when the surge begins immediately after organizers start promoting the connection," the report states.

"These influence actions are cognitive warfare. Foreign actors don't need Americans to become pro-China," Rob Joyce, former director of cybersecurity at the National Security Agency, told Fox News Digital. "They need Americans to argue for the outcomes Beijing wants. And a free society that can't build the power and govern the advanced technology is going to wind up renting it from the adversary, read the PRC, that doesn't share its own values. And that scares me as an American."

DOJ LAUNCHES GRAND JURY PROBE INTO MARXIST MOGUL NEVILLE ROY SINGHAM'S FUNDING OF LEFTIST GROUPS

The report identifies at least a year of coordination among far-left activists in the Singham network, deliberately linking the issues through propaganda media outlets and activist networks funded and supported by Singham.

Late last September, BreakThrough News laid the groundwork, publishing an article that described Flock as "America’s authoritarian tracking infrastructure." Soon after, People’s Dispatch, now merged into the BreakThrough News operations, covered a Denver campaign against data centers the next month, using a photograph from the Party for Socialism and Liberation’s Denver chapter and quoting a local Party for Socialism and Liberation organizer.

By early May, the Party for Socialism and Liberation’s Denver chapter partnered with Indivisible and the far-left Sunrise Movement and promoted a forum examining the "connections between mass surveillance and data centers and how BOTH only serve the needs of billionaires and not our communities."

PROBE INTO 'SUBVERSIVE' ANTI-AI SINGHAM NETWORK IS 'ENORMOUS,' FORMER TREASURY ADVISOR SAYS

Days later, on May 19, when the convergence of issues went public, the local Denver chapter of the Party for Socialism and Liberation circulated a petition to urge the Denver city council to block the building of data centers, arguing, "FIGHTING BACK AGAINST DATA CENTERS MEANS FIGHTING FOR SOCIALISM!" It also posted photos opposing Flock cameras.

On July 11, in Charlotte, N.C., the Party for Socialism and Liberation’s local chapter published an anti-Flock post centered on "AI mass surveillance" and police "brutality," then directed readers to sign a North Carolina petition opposing data-center construction on a dedicated website, nodatacentersnc.com, anonymously purchased the month earlier on June 19, according to online records.

By July 25, in Tucson, Ariz., the local Party for Socialism and Liberation chapter joined "deFLOCK Tucson" and the "No Desert Data Center Coalition" for an event called "It’s ALL Connected" at the "Global Justice Center" on E. 26th Street.

The promotional material asked what mass surveillance, data centers and electric power had in common. The answer: "IT’S ALL CONNECTED."

The report says the campaigns combine concerns over water, electricity rates, land use, noise, health, immigration enforcement, policing and artificial intelligence. Those concerns can be legitimate, the report notes, but organizers can also use them to make the broader infrastructure supporting American computing appear inherently dangerous or illegitimate.

In July, CodePink’s Detroit chapter published a description of data centers as the physical infrastructure of mass surveillance, linking them to OpenAI, Palantir Technologies, military contractors and ICE, crafting a narrative around the argument that the AI data center industry "creates harm and destruction."

CodePink has dedicated a website page to a new campaign, "DATA CENTERS AND THE WAR ECONOMY," describing data centers as products and instruments of war and warning that projects "must be halted wherever they are." Its action page calls on activists to build a joint struggle against data centers and the "war economy."

TEXAS GOV. GREG ABBOTT MOVES TO CUT STATE FUNDING FOR AI-POWERED FLOCK CAMERAS AMID PRIVACY CONCERNS

Flock cameras provide a particularly effective local "entry grievances," according to the report. A dispute over a police contract, a license-plate reader or a single alleged misuse can be expanded into a broader argument about databases, artificial intelligence, cloud systems and data centers.

"Flock gives that abstraction a visible local target," the report states, allowing organizers to portray "a much larger infrastructure buildout" as threatening.

Flock’s actual computing footprint is small, according to company officials. According to Rahul Sidhu, chief strategy officer at Flock, the company uses less than 0.1% of the capacity of a single data center. But the report argues that Flock’s political value is far greater than its computational footprint because it gives the "surveillance state" argument a concrete and emotionally potent target.

Ultimately, the causes have converged, say experts, with Republican politicians joining the chorus of criticism by pro-China communists in recent days against data centers and Flock cameras. As the Party for Socialism and Liberation continued to rail against "AI mass surveillance," DeSantis this week opposed the rise of an "AI digital surveillance state."

The renewed scrutiny on the Singham network’s alleged influence operations on local communities emerges as it faces serious investigation by Congress and federal investigators. The Senate Judiciary Committee previously asked the Justice Department and FBI to assess whether CodePink and the People’s Forum should register under the Foreign Agents Registration Act, called FARA.

The House Oversight Committee has sought records concerning Singham’s funding relationships, while the House Ways and Means Committee recently sent subpoenas to BreakThrough News, Tricontinental and the People’s Forum, which have refused to supply documents, saying they are the targets of a "witch hunt."

As Fox News Digital first reported in late June, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York launched a grand jury investigation earlier this year that is examining possible money laundering, wire fraud and bank fraud violations by Singham and the network of nonprofits he funded.

item.title: India's Modi-Iran meeting comes amid US warnings of sanctions on Tehran's trading partners
item.description: Trump administration Iran sanctions threaten India's commercial and energy ties with Tehran, putting India-U.S. relations to the test over secondary sanctions.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration is ramping up economic sanctions on Iran through "Operation Economic Outcast," while also threatening dire secondary sanctions against countries that continue Iran-related business.

The new policy puts countries like India and other close U.S. partners in an awkward situation.

New Delhi remains a critical U.S. partner in the Indo-Pacific, but it also has commercial, energy and strategic interests in Iran that it won't likely discard, potentially putting it at odds with the Trump administration.

TRUMP THREATENS 'UNPRECEDENTED' ECONOMIC CONSEQUENCES FOR ANY NATION AIDING IRAN

On Monday, exactly a week after the Trump administration launched its new sanctions campaign, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan. It was their first meeting since the war broke out six months ago.

According to an Iranian readout, Pezeshkian asked Modi "to use India’s extensive contacts" to help steer the involved parties away from war and back toward dialogue, while thanking Modi for standing by Tehran. Modi reiterated that New Delhi wants to strengthen its "long-standing friendship" with Tehran and "expand and diversify" the two countries’ trade basket.

"That was for Modi to signal to a domestic audience that he is not kowtowing to Trump," Council on Foreign Relations Senior Fellow Sadanand Dhume told Fox News Digital. "India-Iran relations have already been largely hollowed out by previous rounds of sanctions, so there is no question of India trying to balance between the U.S. and Iran," he added.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio was asked by Fox News' Brian Kilmeade on "The Brian Kilmeade Show" Tuesday about Modi's meeting with the Iranian president.

Rubio said he didn't think there was a trade deal between India and Iran — noting many countries around the world talk to Tehran — and stated, "What ultimately happens, though, is – and the President’s been very clear – is no country should be helping Iran evade sanctions. No country should be out there helping them create mechanisms by which they can generate revenue that they will then use to sponsor terrorism and try to build a nuclear weapon. And if countries decide to do that, then we’re going to have to sanction them too."


A U.S. official echoed Rubio's comments and told Fox News Digital that, "the Administration continues to have positive discussions with our economic partners to ensure Iran never possesses a nuclear weapon."

India has been among Iran’s top five trading partners in recent years, though bilateral trade has dropped dramatically since its 2018-19 peak.

IRAN LOSES KEY ECONOMIC LIFELINE IN MIDDLE EAST THAT TRUMP'S SANCTIONS COULDN'T REACH AS DEADLOCK PERSISTS

New Delhi’s exports to Iran are concentrated on goods that can carry humanitarian exemptions, including pharmaceuticals. Iran is also the second-largest overseas market for Indian rice, with India exporting more than $383 million worth in the first six months of the year.

Conversely, India resumed importing Iranian crude oil for the first time in seven years in April, after the Trump administration temporarily lifted sanctions to soften the Middle East conflict’s impact on global energy. Iranian oil shipments to India were valued at roughly $707 million in the first half of the year.

India has already come into the Treasury Department's crosshairs, with the U.S. sanctioning four India-based companies and three Indian nationals over alleged links to Iranian petroleum and petrochemical trade.

The Treasury Department says countries will receive a defined timeline to shut down Iran-related activity as identified by Washington. That puts banks, shippers, insurers and trade intermediaries on notice before any further penalties are imposed. The United Arab Emirates’ suspension of commercial and financial dealings with Iran has already squeezed Indian exporters, as Dubai has long served as a key hub for trade with Iran.

IRAN DEAL CLOCK HITS ZERO AS TRUMP DEMANDS ‘WHITE FLAG’ WITH NEW PRESSURE CAMPAIGN LOOMING

So far, Washington’s initial actions have stopped short of targeting India’s wider commercial relationship with Iran.

Iran, meanwhile, has warned of "grave consequences" for countries that cooperate with what it calls illegal U.S. behavior.

India's interests in Iran also run beyond commerce. The Chabahar port, Iran’s only oceanic port, supports trade routes linking India to Central Asia and Europe through Iran, while bypassing Pakistan. It also gives India an access route to Central Asia that bypasses Pakistan. But U.S. sanctions uncertainty has repeatedly complicated India’s operations there.

India, the world's third-biggest oil importer and consumer, has already faced the cost of the Middle East conflict, through energy disruptions, higher import costs and inflation. It has also shown it will resist U.S. pressure when core interests are at stake. 

For instance, it has defended ties with Russia, despite Moscow’s adversarial relationship with Washington. But experts argue Iran no longer carries the same weight.

"The Russian example is strikingly different. New Delhi shares close military and diplomatic ties with Moscow that are much more important to India than its ties with Iran, notwithstanding lip service to the latter," Dhume said. "Higher global oil prices hurt India, but India weaned itself off Iranian oil imports a while back."

For the U.S., squeezing major economies like India over their ties to Tehran could pose a diplomatic risk. U.S. national security officials stress the need for a workable strategic relationship with India, especially to counterbalance Chinese power.

Under President Trump’s second term, once-blooming U.S.-India relations have been under strain. Trump and Modi sought to reset the relationship just months ago, but the latest Iran sanctions could test it again.

But the U.S. retains enormous leverage over India, particularly when it comes to trade.

"If forced to choose, New Delhi will obviously and emphatically choose its valuable commercial relationship with the U.S. over its skimpy trade ties with the Islamic republic," Dhume said.

The timing is notable, with Chinese President Xi Jinping reportedly set to visit India for next week’s BRICS summit. Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are also expected to attend.

Analysts say the impact will ultimately depend on how aggressively Washington moves from warnings and diplomacy to actual secondary sanctions. That is particularly true with India, where more aggressive enforcement risks further straining U.S. relations with a strategically important partner.

"The U.S. should learn from its own past success in quietly persuading India to generally kick its Iran oil habit," Dhume said. "Quiet diplomacy works better with India than bluster. This is the key lesson from the past that the Trump administration appears to be forgetting."

The Indian government did not respond to Fox News Digital requests for comment.

item.title: Viral video of jets buzzing DHL Stadium in Cape Town prompts aviation safety investigation
item.description: Viral video shows two Embraer E-Jets barely clearing DHL Stadium in South Africa before a Springboks vs. All Blacks rugby match in Cape Town.
item.content:encoded:
Last week, fans at a rugby match between South Africa and New Zealand got a show before the opening... uh... however it is that rugby matches start when a pair of Embraer E-Jets flew over the stadium.

Barely over the stadium.

Video of the moment quickly went viral, and it left a lot of people thinking, "Hey, that was very cool, but it seems like that may have been a little too low."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Well, despite some evidence that these low flyovers have happened before in South Africa, the stadium tower buzzing is now under investigation.

"It is therefore critical that we interrogate this past weekend’s events … to determine if there were any safety concerns which warrant a review," The South African Civil Aviation Authority (SACAA) said in a statement, per the Associated Press.

The flyover came just before the start of a match in the "Rugby's Greatest Rivalry" series that pits the Springboks against the All Blacks in matches around the world. This one in particular was in Cape Town and featured the two Airlink-operated jets flying over the city's DHL Stadium.

The airline was reportedly set to do another flyover at a match in Soweto, but has dropped those plans.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

It's good to at least take a look at this because if they weren't supposed to be flying that low, something needs to be done... but, man, that was cool.

There's just something about a flyover. I see planes fly over my house all the time, but when I saw a B-2 bomber soar over the Freedom 250 Grand Prix recently, it was like reaching another state of technologically advanced, radar-avoiding nirvana.

So, while safety has to be the number one priority, let's make sure we never do away with the wonders of having jets fly over stadiums full of people.

item.title: 2028 Dem hopeful's longtime ally exposed for deep ties to CCP officials: 'Good friends'
item.description: Rep. Ro Khanna's, D-Calif. former senior advisor on foreign trade and economic development could be liability to a potential 2028 campaign due to his ties to CCP officials.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., has been floated as a potential 2028 Democratic contender for president, but his longtime ally and former senior advisor on foreign trade and economic development could be a liability due to his deep ties to Chinese Communist Party officials, a Fox News Digital investigation found.

Henry Yin is a longtime California businessman and political operative who Khanna has praised for his "leadership" and has called one of his "good friends" on Facebook. He was born in China, raised in Taiwan and then moved to the United States, where he has lived for several decades.

However, while living in California, Yin has been a major player helping China get a foothold in California over the last several decades through multiple roles, including serving as a member of the California Commission for Economic Development and founding a consulting firm that included multiple corporate clients with ties to Chinese Communist Party officials. 

A 2011 profile piece revealed that Yin "made his fortune selling used computer equipment to China" and had "done business in China for more than a quarter-century." The profile piece went on to say Yin has "good connections and a sense of [China's] business climate" and was "leading city trade delegations to China, which have contributed to several Chinese firms — most recently software company Trunkbow International — setting up offices in the city and helping city businessmen get a foothold in China."

SWALWELL RESIGNATION COLLIDES WITH CHINA-LINKED SCANDAL AS CRITICS DEMAND FILE RELEASE

"Henry has some sort of special skill-building relationships," one businessman said in the profile piece, praising Yin. "There’s a lot more government involvement in China, and you need relationships with local government officials."

In addition to his consulting business and several overseas trips to China, Yin has allegedly attended at least 10 events hosted by United Front groups, including the All-China Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese (ACFROC), according to China expert Jackie Deal, the president of Long Term Strategy Group, a defense research firm. Fox News Digital has extensively reported on the CCP's United Front and the threat it poses to U.S. institutions as the CCP gains influence in the United States.

In a Sept. 2019 Facebook post, Khanna announced that Yin, who was first appointed to the California Commission for Economic Development in 2010 by then- Republican Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger and later reappointed to the position in 2015 by the succeeding Democratic Gov. Jerry Brown, would "serve as my Senior Advisor on Foreign Trade and Economic Development."

"We discussed the importance of improving the US China relationship to cooperate on issues of climate change and medical research while protecting intellectual property and opening access to markets," Khanna continued. "I was particularly touched that Henry and the group had a birthday cake for me. It was wonderful celebrating with them!"

A few months later, in December of the same year, Khanna posted about Yin on Facebook again, writing, "Thank you Henry Yin for your leadership!" 

That same month, Yin invited Khanna to be his "honorable guest" for an event titled, "S.V. U.S.-China Trading Partners Concerned Group Dinner Meeting Agenda," which was sponsored by Yin's consulting firm, USA-China-Link. A review of the event's presentations showed the attendees were slated to talk about an array of topics, including China investments, technology and business asset management, among other topics. Khanna was slated to discuss intellectual property.

ELITE US COLLEGES LINKED TO CHINESE SURVEILLANCE LABS DRIVING UYGHUR ‘GENOCIDE,’ STUDY WARNS

In Feb. 2020, Khanna posted another photo of himself having dinner with Yin, who he referred to as one of his "good friends." In the post, Khanna decried that "Chinese Americans are feeling they are being stereotyped as the symbols for the coronavirus." 

"This is a time to embrace our Chinese American neighbors and friends and continue to frequent Chinese-American stores, restaurants and shopping centers." 

On Yin's LinkedIn profile, which still includes the senior advisor title with Khanna's office, he includes over a dozen slides detailing his consulting business, USA-China-Link, and showcasing his business acumen in China, which was featured in several profile pieces in Chinese state media. One of the slides says his firm "specialized in high-tech and green tech" and helped China do business in California and vice versa. Other slides show a list of his Chinese clients and a slide that called him an "Official Commerce Rep in US for the Province of Fujian, China."

Another slide shows a photo of Yin at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing in 2009 for the China National Day Banquet, where he calls himself a "VIP" in the caption. According to reports on the event, the banquet included several senior-level CCP officials in attendance, including then-Chinese President Hu Jintao and his successor Xi Jinping, the former third-ranking member of the CCP's Politburo Standing Committee, Wen Jiabao, among other top officials.

A spokesperson for Khanna, who is a member of the House Select Committee on the CCP, told Fox News Digital earlier this year that "Henry Yin has never been employed by Rep. Khanna" and "he doesn’t serve in any role in his office or campaign." When asked Wednesday whether his office stands by the quote, Khanna's office did not immediately respond. Despite the previous denial, Khanna and Yin were pictured sitting beside each other earlier this year at an event.

In Feb. 2026, Khanna posted a photo showing him sitting beside Yin at a political action committee meeting in Sunnyvale, California. Khanna wrote he was "honored to be back in the district, hearing directly from Chinese American community leaders."

Yin has made several trips abroad to China over the last decade, including a July trip where he led a delegation to Guangzhou to meet with Zhu Xiaojun, the Department of Commerce of Guangdong Province's deputy director, which is a CCP-controlled position. A Chinese report on the trip said the two sides collaborated on two-way trade between California and the Guangdong province. Two months before the event, Yin attended the 2026 China-California Economic and Trade Forum, which was hosted by the Chinese Consulate in Los Angeles and included multiple CCP officials in attendance.

He also accompanied California Gov. Gavin Newsom in late 2023 for a delegation, where he served as an advisor, according to another Chinese media report. During the trip, Newsom would meet with top CCP officials, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Wang Yi, who has been a CCP member since 1981 and is currently serving as a "Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, and Minister of Foreign Affairs." Newsom also met with Han Zheng, China's vice president.

A Fox News Digital review of Yin's Facebook account also unearthed other China trips he made, including Chinese delegations he has helped host in California. In 2014, Yin signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) between the California Green Tech Center and China Venture Capital Association, which appeared to be one of his firm's clients. Other posts show multiple China visits, including the 2015 "China South Asia Expo," which featured a speech from the now-former Chinese Vice President Li Yuanchao. A 2019 post highlights another China trip he took, which he called "fruitful" and included over a dozen photos of Chinese officials he met with. One of the photos included the names of Chinese and American companies where he was facilitating trade projects. 

ELITE US COLLEGES LINKED TO CHINESE SURVEILLANCE LABS DRIVING UYGHUR ‘GENOCIDE,’ STUDY WARNS

A Fox News Digital investigation also unearthed a 2013 photo that appears to show Christine "Fang Fang" Fang — the Chinese spy at the center of the scandal involving disgraced former Rep. Eric Swalwell — alongside key political figures. Posing together at a public gathering, Fang stood behind then-Chinese Consul General to San Francisco Gao Zhansheng and top leaders from the Asian Pacific Islander American Public Affairs Association (APAPA), including Yin.

A recently declassified FBI report on Swalwell's ties to Fang Fang revealed that a "prominent businessman in the Bay Area" tied to APAPA introduced Swalwell to Fang Fang. While Fox News Digital could not confirm whether the redacted section of the FBI report was referring to Yin, or potentially his brother, C.C., who founded APAPA and opened up several McDonald's franchises, Axios previously quoted Yin saying that Fang Fang was "very active" with the APAPA Bay Area chapter and remembered seeing her at several events.

The photo was originally shared on Facebook in February 2013 by the late Don Sun, a prominent California civic leader and tech executive who passed away in 2024. In the photo caption, Sun wrote that the Yin family and APAPA had thrown a farewell dinner for the Chinese consul at San Francisco’s Embarcadero Center. Sun said the photo depicts the consul and "all my friends at APAPA."

UNEARTHED PHOTO OF SWALWELL MEETING WITH TOP CCP OFFICIAL RAISES ALARM BELLS: 'VERY DISTURBING'

An APAPA spokesperson confirmed that Yin is a current member of the group's board. The spokesperson wrote in an emailed statement earlier this year that the photo "appears to reflect a private gathering and does not represent APAPA programming, partnerships, or operations." They emphasized that attendance by individual members of APAPA at events "does not reflect organizational positions, affiliations, or activities beyond that context."

"Public officials should strongly scrutinize any APAPA efforts that align with CCP objectives, including the CCP influence operations to prevent data center construction across America," Michael Lucci, the CEO of State Armor, a nonprofit countering CCP threats, told the New York Post.

"APAPA does not have documentation to substantiate the characterization in Mr. Sun’s post that the dinner was ‘co-hosted’ by APAPA, and we cannot validate third party descriptions of the event based on a photo and a social media caption," the spokesperson said, adding, "Individuals may attend events in a personal capacity, and such attendance should not be construed as an organizational activity or endorsement."

The spokesperson also noted that "APAPA has no records indicating that he [Yin] has served as a senior advisor to Rep. Khanna" despite an APAPA press release from January 2022 announcing Yin joining the group's national governing board and states that he "has served as Senior Advisor to U.S. Representative Ro Khanna, who represents the South Bay Area." 

Pressed by Fox News Digital on this, the APAPA spokesperson said, "The current APAPA headquarters leadership and team had no knowledge of, and do not maintain any records confirming, Mr. Henry Yin serving as a senior advisor to Rep. Khanna. APAPA does not oversee, verify, or maintain records related to an individual’s outside titles or roles with public officials."

They added that "With respect to historical references appearing on legacy APAPA web pages or posts, APAPA is in the process of reviewing and removing outdated or inaccurate content that does not reflect current leadership, governance, or verified records." They added that "questions regarding any past or current status with Rep. Khanna’s office should be directed to that office or to Mr. Yin directly."

Yin did not respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment.
